$comment: Support merger golden dataset. Each case: a mixed staff question, the analyst's reply and the policy assistant's reply exactly as they might come back - including the noise the merge exists to remove, a sentence where one side says it knows nothing about the half the other side answered. 'mustContain' is what the one merged answer has to keep (facts from both sides, and every citation); 'mustNotContain' is the noise it has to drop. Matching is case-insensitive. A merge that loses a citation is thrown away by the merger itself and the two replies are shown as they were; that fallback counts as a failure here, because it means the model did not do the job. Two cases come from a live run with a four-question paragraph: 'analyst-invents-a-rule' - the analyst, which never sees the rule documents, answered a rule question from nowhere and the merge kept it, uncited; and 'name-the-unanswered-part' - a bare 'no information on this' that left the reader guessing which part it meant.
